title: Medicines and glomerular pressure
model: Qualitative haemodynamic tendencies; independent, context-specific comparisons

scenes.title: ANGIOTENSIN II
scenes.mechanism: Preferential efferent constriction supports glomerular pressure.
scenes.context: Moderate activation illustrated; strong activation can constrict both sides.

scenes.title: ACE INHIBITORS
scenes.mechanism: Less angiotensin II formation → efferent relaxation.
scenes.context: Acute GFR may fall; albuminuric kidney disease can benefit long term.

layout.caption: Less angiotensin II → efferent relaxation.
layout.context: An initial GFR dip can accompany long-term benefit.

scenes.title: ANGIOTENSIN RECEPTOR BLOCKERS
scenes.mechanism: AT1 receptor blockade → less efferent constrictor tone.
scenes.context: A similar haemodynamic endpoint to ACE inhibition, via a different target.

layout.caption: AT1 blockade → less efferent constrictor tone.

scenes.title: PROSTAGLANDIN SUPPORT
scenes.mechanism: PGE2 and PGI2 help preserve afferent dilation and renal perfusion.
scenes.context: This endogenous support matters most when perfusion is threatened.

layout.caption: PGE2 / PGI2 help maintain afferent dilation.

scenes.title: NSAIDs
scenes.mechanism: COX inhibition removes vasodilator support → afferent constriction.
scenes.context: The haemodynamic AKI risk is greater with low effective circulating volume.

layout.caption: COX inhibition removes afferent vasodilator support.
layout.context: AKI risk is greater when perfusion is low.

scenes.title: SGLT2 INHIBITORS: FEEDBACK
scenes.mechanism: More NaCl reaches the macula densa → tubuloglomerular feedback.
scenes.context: Restored afferent tone lowers intraglomerular pressure and hyperfiltration.

layout.caption: More NaCl at the macula densa → restored feedback.

scenes.title: SGLT2 INHIBITORS: CONTEXT MATTERS
scenes.mechanism: Post-glomerular dilation can also contribute to the pressure reduction.
scenes.context: Effects vary by setting; an early GFR dip can accompany long-term kidney benefit.

layout.caption: Post-glomerular dilation can also lower pressure.
layout.context: Effects vary by setting; an early dip can accompany long-term benefit.

scenes.title: WHEN THE EFFECTS COMBINE
scenes.reference:
Volume depletion, e.g.
with diuretic use
scenes.mechanism: Low perfusion + NSAID afferent constriction + ACEi OR ARB efferent dilation.
scenes.context: A volume-depleting diuretic effect is indirect—not selective arteriolar constriction.

layout.caption: Low perfusion, a tighter inlet and a more relaxed outlet.
